newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Globus says '96 profits down as planned.
newsitem.headline: Globus says '96 profits down as planned.

text.p: Hungarian canned food and fruit juice maker Globus Rt said on Friday that its 1996 after-tax profit slightly exceeded the plan despite a drastic fall in domestic demand for its products.
Globus said earlier on Friday that its after-tax profit dropped to 171.2 million forints in 1996 from 248 million in 1995, but was four percent higher than the company had planned.
The company said its 1996 results were depressed by falling domestic consumption due to a slump in real wages since 1995 when Hungary introduced a strict economic austerity programme.
Private consumption in Hungary fell some four percent in 1996, but is seen remaining stable or slightly rising this year.
"(Consumption trends in 1996) reflected sharply falling demand in the food industry," Globus said in a statement.
"The drop in real wages triggered a 25 to 30 percent drop in processed food retail sales,"

The company set off part of this unfavourable effect by only moderate price rises, while it also cut costs and increased its export sales, mainly in the Community of Independent States (CIS) and the Baltic states, Globus said.
The weight of exports within total sales rose to 26.7 percent in 1996 from some 17 percent in 1995, it said.
The company added that it cut the number of its employees to 527 in 1996 from 804 the year before.
Globus was trading at 1,680 forints, down 20, on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Friday.
